title: Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
hook: muP lets you tune hyperparameters on a small model and transfer them to a huge one. This paper derives the equivalent rules for gated delta networks, so sub-quadratic models scale without re-tuning.
key_points: Sub-quadratic linear architectures are cheaper than Transformers but lack principled scaling rules.
Maximal Update Parametrization (muP) gives zero-shot hyperparameter transfer — but didn't extend to these models.
Derives scaling rules for Gated Delta Networks by tracking coordinate sizes through forward pass, gates, and recurrence.
Pre-training experiments confirm stable learning-rate transfer across widths under both AdamW and SGD.
content_html: Training large language models is expensive, which drives interest in both sub-quadratic architectures (cheaper than attention) and principled ways to pick hyperparameters without re-tuning at every scale. The Maximal Update Parametrization (muP) solved the latter for standard Transformers — letting you transfer hyperparameters zero-shot across model widths — but extending it to linear models with structured state transitions and intricate gating had stayed largely unexplored.
extra_html: Liu and Gu derive the scaling rules for the Gated Delta Network by rigorously propagating coordinate-size estimates through the forward pass, the gating mechanisms, and the recurrent state dynamics. Language-model pre-training experiments confirm that their configurations enable stable learning-rate transfer across model widths under both AdamW and SGD, whereas standard parametrization fails to transfer — evidence that the analysis is both correct and practically useful. The upshot: a recipe for scaling these efficient architectures without redoing hyperparameter search at full size. See the arXiv link for the derivations.

related.title: Subquadratic Architectures: xLSTM vs. Mamba-2 vs. Gated DeltaNet
related.hook: Transformers pay a quadratic tax on sequence length. Pitting xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet head-to-head on hard tasks, xLSTM comes out ahead — and the paper explains why.

flashcards.back_html: muP enables zero-shot hyperparameter transfer across model widths. Its extension to linear models with structured state transitions was largely unexplored — this paper fills that gap.
